name: pdk-st2-resumable-execution-stream
instr:
# Resumable execution stream

The UI and ChatOps clients need to follow execution results across reconnects and st2stream replicas. Extend the existing `/v1/stream` SSE interface for execution and liveaction state changes.

- Every `st2.execution__create/update` and `st2.liveaction__create/update` delivery carries a positive, monotonically increasing numeric SSE `id`, shared across producers; its JSON `data` represents the state at that change. In particular, scheduled, running and succeeded transitions for one execution arrive in order, without an older state following a newer one when cancellation overlaps a late running-status write.
- `Last-Event-ID` resumes after that ID on either replica: replay all retained missed changes exactly once, in ID order, then continue live without a gap or duplicate, including after a stream process is killed. `Last-Event-ID: 0` requests replay from the start of the retained history when the beginning is still available. A cursor older than the retained window returns an explicit `resync` SSE event instead of silently skipping changes. The retention window is the latest 16 execution/liveaction changes; cursors before that window resync.
- The API's `POST /v1/executions`, `POST /v1/executions/{id}/re_run`, `PUT /v1/executions/{id}` and `DELETE /v1/executions/{id}` transitions use the same stream contract. Existing clients without `Last-Event-ID` continue receiving live updates with the existing SSE event names, JSON `id` and `status` fields,
